lines.trans: Girls walking around in tiny outfits like that just come right out on television nowadays!
What? Oh dear, what do we do, honey!
If those young women fall head over heels for our Seung-chan and throw themselves at him…
Oh boy, that would be serious trouble!
Right when I might win a party nomination for Yeouido…
if that son of mine gets caught up in even a tiny scandal, that would be fatal!
Even if I put myself in that female celebrity's shoes…
once anyone lays eyes on our Seung-chan, they are bound to fall head over heels!

words.gloss: is destined to, I tell you!

lines.trans: We cannot just stop sending him to work at the broadcasting station.
and we cannot make him walk around covering his face either.

examples.text: 저런 거지 같은 설명에도 우리 신디가 맞혔다고!
examples.trans: Even with a terrible explanation like that, our Cindy got it right!
Here the word for 'that kind of' is key.

examples.text: 저런 짧은 옷만 입고 돌아다니는 애들이 티브이에 막 나오고 저러니!
examples.trans: Girls walking around in tiny outfits like that just come right out on television nowadays!

examples.text: 오늘도 저런 짧은 옷만 입고 돌아다니는 애들이 티브이에 막 나오고 저러니!
examples.trans: short, skimpy in everyday conversation
The outfit you're wearing today is really pretty.
It's cold, so please wear warm clothes.

meanings.note: Used for clothing worn on the body (shirts, pants, dresses, outfits).

examples.trans: I wore a black coat today.
It's cold, so please dress warmly.

examples.text: 저런 짧은 옷만 입고 돌아다니는 애들이 티브이에 막 나오고 저러니!
examples.trans: Girls walking around in tiny outfits like that just come right out on television nowadays!
This expression comes from 'going around'.

meanings.note: Colloquially used to refer to people of the same age or younger.

examples.trans: Kids are running around and playing in the park.
That person has a really good personality.

examples.text: 티브이도 잘 안 보시는구나. 오늘 여러모로 굴욕을 많이 당하네요.
examples.trans: You don't watch television much either. I am suffering humiliation in many ways today.
The topic of television too came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: used in 막을 내리다 / 막 내리다 ('to bring down the curtain', i.e., to end a show or era)

examples.trans: The performance came to an end.
The stage curtain went up.

meanings.en: to appear, be published, be achieved (a score/result)
meanings.note: Used for ratings, test scores, or results coming out

examples.trans: I came outside from the house.
The exam results came out well.

examples.text: 저런 짧은 옷만 입고 돌아다니는 애들이 티브이에 막 나오고 저러니!
examples.trans: Girls walking around in tiny outfits like that just come right out on television nowadays!
This expression comes from 'acting like that!'.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?
dummy trans 1
dummy trans 2

meanings.en: what to do, how to act

examples.trans: What should we do?
What should we do? (2)
What? Oh dear, what do we do, honey!
Here the word for 'honey, dear!' is key.

examples.text: 여자애들이 우리 승찬이한테 푹 빠져가지고 막 들이대고 그러면,
examples.trans: If those young women fall head over heels for our Seung-chan and throw themselves at him…
Here the word for 'young women' is key.

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.

examples.text: 여자애들이 우리 승찬이한테 푹 빠져가지고 막 들이대고 그러면,
examples.trans: If those young women fall head over heels for our Seung-chan and throw themselves at him…
Here the word for 'deeply, head over heels' is key.

examples.text: 일반인 훈남한테 빠진 톱스타 같은 거네요?
examples.trans: So it's like a top star falling for an ordinary handsome guy?

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 빠지다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (fallen for).

examples.text: 여자애들이 우리 승찬이한테 푹 빠져가지고 막 들이대고 그러면,
examples.trans: If those young women fall head over heels for our Seung-chan and throw themselves at him…
This expression comes from 'come on strong and'.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.
Oh boy, that would be serious trouble!
Here the word for 'oh dear, oh boy' is key.
Then let's meet tomorrow.
Then we're at the same company!
Oh boy, that would be serious trouble!
Here the word for 'big trouble!' is key.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.
What time is it now?
I'll leave right now.

examples.text: 내가 여의도에 지금 공천을 받을지도 모르는 이 상황에,
examples.trans: Right when I might win a party nomination for Yeouido…
Here the word for 'party nomination' is key.

meanings.note: Used for gifts, money, messages, or documents.

examples.trans: I received a birthday present.
Please answer the phone.

meanings.en: to not know, to be unaware of
meanings.note: 르-irregular verb: stem 모르- + -아요/-았어요 → 몰라요 / 몰랐어요.

examples.trans: I don't know well either.
I didn't realize time was passing.

meanings.note: demonstrative determiner placed before a noun

examples.text: 이 바닥은 자기 밥그릇은 자기가 챙겨야 돼.
examples.trans: In this industry, you have to look after your own rice bowl.
This book is interesting.
Situation is good.
Situation is bad.
Did you hear about this son?
I was busy today because of son.

examples.text: 아들이란 녀석이 조그만 스캔들에라도 휘말리면 이거 치명적인데!
examples.trans: if that son of mine gets caught up in even a tiny scandal, that would be fatal!
Here the word for 'chap, fellow' is key.

examples.text: 아들이란 녀석이 조그만 스캔들에라도 휘말리면 이거 치명적인데!
examples.trans: if that son of mine gets caught up in even a tiny scandal, that would be fatal!

examples.text: 아들이란 녀석이 조그만 스캔들에라도 휘말리면 이거 치명적인데!
examples.trans: if that son of mine gets caught up in even a tiny scandal, that would be fatal!

examples.text: 아들이란 녀석이 조그만 스캔들에라도 휘말리면 이거 치명적인데!
examples.trans: if that son of mine gets caught up in even a tiny scandal, that would be fatal!
This expression comes from 'if he gets swept up'.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun for something near the speaker; often contracted to 이거 in speech.

examples.trans: Did you film this too?
How much is this?

examples.text: 아들이란 녀석이 조그만 스캔들에라도 휘말리면 이거 치명적인데!
examples.trans: if that son of mine gets caught up in even a tiny scandal, that would be fatal!
Here the word for 'would be fatal!' is key.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.
Did you hear about this female?
I was busy today because of female.
Did you hear about this celebrity?
I was busy today because of celebrity.
Even if I put myself in that female celebrity's shoes…
Here the word for 'even in the position of' is key.

meanings.en: first of all, for starters, for the time being
meanings.note: marks an immediate first step before dealing with anything else

examples.trans: Let's sit down and talk first.
Let's wait until today for now.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)

meanings.note: Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그 아이 ('that child/kid'); used only for younger people or close peers.

examples.trans: Are you close with her?
He is late every day.

related.gloss: this kid / he or she (near speaker)
that kid / he or she (over there)

meanings.note: Softens a statement or downplays a motive.

examples.trans: I just asked out of curiosity.
I'll just stay home today.
I have to go to the TV station this afternoon.
Fans are waiting in front of the broadcasting station.

출근.gloss: going to work, attendance at work

meanings.en: going to work, reporting for work

examples.trans: I get to work by 9 a.m.
I'm nervous because it's my first day at work.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.en: to make someone do, to assign work
meanings.note: Causative verb; e.g., 일을 시키다 'to assign work'.
E.g., 치킨을 시키다 'to order fried chicken'.

examples.trans: The team leader assigned this work to me.
Shall we order pizza for dinner?

meanings.note: Bound noun used in -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다 ('can / cannot').

examples.trans: I can read Korean.
I cannot go today.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.
Did you hear about this face, though?
I was busy today because of face, though.
and we cannot make him walk around covering his face either.
This expression comes from 'covering and'.

meanings.en: to go around, to attend, to commute
meanings.note: Indicates regular movement or carrying something around constantly.

examples.trans: I commute to the company.
I carry a bag around with me.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?
